subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw core sponsor a first-class Gateway control-plane and per-agent runtime split, and what narrow milestone should be approved first?
rationale: The RFC would define public runtime protocol, config, lifecycle, session-state, and security-boundary contracts; automation can verify the gap but cannot choose the product and trust model safely.

options.title: Approve a narrow Phase 0/1 design
options.body: Keep embedded mode as default and first specify per-agent lifecycle plus local process/runtime protocol boundaries before container or Kubernetes execution.

options.title: Defer to backend/profile slices
options.body: Use this RFC as context while maintainers review the narrower subagent execution-backend tracker and implementation PR first.

options.title: Pause distributed runtime core work
options.body: Do not sponsor core distributed-runtime work until gateway stability and setup priorities move further along.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow Phase 0/1 design
recommendation.body: Keep embedded mode as default and first specify per-agent lifecycle plus local process/runtime protocol boundaries before container or Kubernetes execution.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent history on the embedded runtime seam and authored the worker-runtime isolation experiment that overlaps this decision.
